\begin{definition}[Query membership]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Query}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Query}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.CVAL, Turing.pairEncode}
For Boolean lists $d$ and $q$, the query relation holds exactly when the encoding of the
pair $(d,q)$ belongs to the fixed language $\mathrm{CVAL}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Query length bounded by data length]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.length_le_of_query}
\label{Complexity.Yap.length_le_of_query}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.size_le_length_encode, Complexity.Yap.Query, Turing.pairEncode_injective}
\difficulty{3}
Let $d$ and $q$ be binary strings. If the pair encoding $\langle d,q\rangle$ is a
yes-instance of the Boolean circuit value language—that is, it encodes a fan-in-two
circuit and an input on which that circuit evaluates to true—then $|q|\le |d|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Evaluation determined by circuit encoding]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.eval_eq_of_encode_eq}
\label{Complexity.Yap.eval_eq_of_encode_eq}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eq_of_encode_eq, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.values}
\difficulty{3}
Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be directed acyclic Boolean circuits, with possibly different
numbers of input bits. If their circuit encodings are equal and their input assignments
have equal associated bit lists, then the circuits evaluate to the same Boolean value on
those assignments.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit query and accepting assignments]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.query_encode_iff}
\label{Complexity.Yap.query_encode_iff}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eq_of_encode_eq, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, Complexity.Yap.Query, Complexity.Yap.eval_eq_of_encode_eq, Turing.pairEncode_injective}
\difficulty{6}
Let $C$ be a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with $n$ input bits, and let $q$ be a bit
string. The query asking whether $C$ accepts $q$ holds exactly when there is an
assignment $x\in\{0,1\}^n$ whose bit string, in order, is $q$ and on which $C$ evaluates
to true.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Circuit query with appended input]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.query_append_iff}
\label{Complexity.Yap.query_append_iff}
\leanok
\uses{BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.IsFaninTwo, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.encode, BoolCircuit.DAGCircuit.eval, Complexity.Yap.Query, Complexity.Yap.query_encode_iff}
\difficulty{5}
Let $m : \mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ let $D_n$ be a
fan-in-two Boolean circuit with $n+m(n)$ input bits. Suppose $z,w$ are bit strings and
$|z|=N$. Then the query asking whether $D_N$ accepts the concatenation $z\mathbin{+\!\!+}w$
holds exactly when there is an assignment $y\in\{0,1\}^{m(|z|)}$ such that $w$ is the
bit string of $y$ in order and $D_{|z|}$ accepts the combined input consisting of $z$
followed by $y$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[One more existential alternation]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.mem_SigmaP_succ_of_exists_le}
\label{Complexity.Yap.mem_SigmaP_succ_of_exists_le}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.KarpLipton.dropMarker, Complexity.KarpLipton.dropMarker_marker, Complexity.KarpLipton.polyTimeComputable_dropMarker, Complexity.PiP, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.comp, Complexity.PolyTimeComputable.pairEncode, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.mem_SigmaP_succ_iff, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairFstD, Complexity.polyTimeComputable_pairSndD, Complexity.preimage_mem_PiP, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{5}
Let $i$ be a natural number and let $L,L'$ be languages of binary strings. Suppose
$L'\in\Pi_i^{\mathsf P}$. If there are natural numbers $B,b$ such that (i) for all
strings $x,u$, membership of $\langle x,u\rangle$ in $L'$ implies $x\in L$, and (ii)
every $x\in L$ has some witness $u$ with $|u|\le B(|x|+1)^b$ and $\langle x,u\rangle\in
L'$, then $L\in\Sigma_{i+1}^{\mathsf P}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Combined natural-number bound]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.nN}
\label{Complexity.Yap.nN}
\leanok
For natural numbers $C_1,c_1,C_2,c_2,n$, define $N$ by
$N=2(2n+2+C_1(n+1)^{c_1})+2+C_2(2n+2+C_1(n+1)^{c_1}+1)^{c_2}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Refutation data]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data}
\leanok
A refutation data package consists of natural-number coefficients $C_1,C_2,C_3,B$,
natural-number degrees $c_1,c_2,c_3,b$, and a language $R$ over Boolean lists. The
fields are designated, respectively, for the two block-length bounds, the
refutation-length bound, the inner-block bound, and the refutation relation.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[First block-length bound]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.M₁}
\leanok
Given a refutation data package and a Boolean list $x$, define the first block-length
bound to be $C_1(|x|+1)^{c_1}$, where $|x|$ is the length of $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Second block-length bound]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.M₂}
\leanok
Given a refutation data package and a Boolean list $y$, define the second block-length
bound to be $C_2(|y|+1)^{c_2}$, where $|y|$ is the length of $y$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Input length parameter]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.nLen}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.nLen}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.nN}
Given a refutation data package and a Boolean list $x$, define its input length
parameter to be the value of the specified function $nN$, evaluated at the package's
coefficients $C_1,c_1,C_2,c_2$ and the length of $x$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Soundness failure witness]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.SoundFail}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.SoundFail}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.M₂, Complexity.Yap.Query, Turing.pairEncode}
Given a refutation data package and Boolean lists $x,U,u,v,w,r$, a soundness-failure
witness consists of all of the following: the length of $v$ equals the package's second
block-length bound evaluated at the encoding of $(x,u)$; the query relation holds for
$U$ and the concatenation of the encoding of $(x,u,v)$ with $w$; the length of $r$ is at
most $C_3$ times one plus the length of the encoding of $(x,u,v)$, raised to $c_3$; and
the encoding of $(x,u,v,r)$ belongs to the package's language $R$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Matching encoded query]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.Match}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.Match}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.M₂, Complexity.Yap.Query, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $d$ be a data structure and let $x,U,u,v,w$ be finite Boolean strings. The predicate
$\text{Match}(x,U,u,v,w)$ holds exactly when the length of $v$ equals $M_2$ applied to
the pair encoding of $x$ and $u$, and the query language $U$ contains the concatenation
of the pair encoding of that encoded pair and $v$ with $w$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Core encoded condition]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.Core}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.Core}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.Match, Complexity.Yap.Data.M₁, Complexity.Yap.Data.SoundFail, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $d$ be a data structure, and let $x,U,t,e$ be finite Boolean strings. The predicate
$\text{Core}(x,U,t,e)$ holds if the first component obtained by taking the first
component of the first component of $t$ has length $M_1(x)$, and either
$\text{SoundFail}$ holds for $x,U$ and the four components of $t$ obtained by the nested
first and second projections, or $\text{Match}$ fails for $x,U$ with that same
first-first component and the two components of $e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Length-bounded check condition]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.Check}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.Check}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.Core, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $d$ be a data structure, and let $w,t,e$ be finite Boolean strings. The predicate
$\text{Check}(w,t,e)$ holds exactly when the length of $t$ is at most $B$ times
$(|w|+1)^b$ and $\text{Core}$ holds for the first and second components of $w$, together
with $t$ and $e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Bad language]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.badLang}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.badLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.Check, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $d$ be a data structure. The bad language consists of the Boolean strings $p$ such
that, for every finite Boolean string $e$ whose length is at most $B(|p|+1)^b$,
$\text{Check}$ holds for the first and second components of $p$ and for $e$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Inner language]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.innerLang}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.innerLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.badLang, Turing.pairEncode}
Let $d$ be a data structure. The inner language consists of the Boolean strings $w$ such
that, for every finite Boolean string $t$, the pair encoding of $w$ and $t$ does not
belong to the bad language.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Check language]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.checkLang}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.checkLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.Check, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
Let $d$ be a data structure. The check language consists of the Boolean strings $q$ for
which $\text{Check}$ holds on the first-first component of $q$, the second component of
its first component, and the second component of $q$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the bad language]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_badLang}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_badLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.Check, Complexity.Yap.Data.badLang, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
\difficulty{1}
For any data object $d$ and bit string $p$, $p$ belongs to the bad language if and only
if every bit string $e$ with length at most $d.B(p.length+1)^{d.b}$ satisfies the check
on the total first and second projections of $p$ and on $e$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the inner language]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_innerLang}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_innerLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.badLang, Complexity.Yap.Data.innerLang, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For any data object $d$ and bit string $w$, $w$ belongs to the inner language exactly
when, for every bit string $t$, the encoding of $(w,t)$ does not belong to the bad
language.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Membership in the check language]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_checkLang}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_checkLang}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.Check, Complexity.Yap.Data.checkLang, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairSndD}
\difficulty{1}
For any data object $d$ and bit string $q$, $q$ belongs to the check language exactly
when $d$'s check holds on the first and second decoded components of the first decoded
component of $q$, and the second decoded component of $q$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Check on an encoded pair]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.check_pair}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.check_pair}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.Check, Complexity.Yap.Data.Core, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
For any data object $d$ and bit strings $x$, $U$, $t$, and $e$, the check on the encoded
pair of $x$ and $U$ holds if and only if $t$ has length at most $d.B$ times the quantity
one plus the length of that encoded pair, raised to $d.b$, and the core condition holds

\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Length of a nested pair encoding]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.Data.length_inst}
\label{Complexity.Yap.Data.length_inst}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data.M₁, Complexity.Yap.Data.M₂, Complexity.Yap.Data.nLen, Complexity.Yap.nN, Turing.length_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}
\difficulty{1}
Let $d$ be a data object with parameters $C_1,c_1,C_2,c_2$, and let $x,u,v$ be finite
bit strings. Suppose $|u|=C_1(|x|+1)^{c_1}$ and $|v|=C_2(|\langle x,u\rangle|+1)^{c_2}$,
where $\langle x,u\rangle$ is the encoding that doubles each bit of $x$, appends the
separator $01$, and then appends $u$. Then $|\langle\langle
x,u\rangle,v\rangle|=2\bigl(2|x|+2+C_1(|x|+1)^{c_1}\bigr)+2+C_2\bigl(2|x|+2+C_1(|x|+1)^{c_1}+1\bigr)^{c_2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Soundness of the inner-language condition]
\lean{Complexity.Yap.sound}
\label{Complexity.Yap.sound}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.Yap.Data, Complexity.Yap.Data.Core, Complexity.Yap.Data.M₁, Complexity.Yap.Data.M₂, Complexity.Yap.Data.check_pair, Complexity.Yap.Data.innerLang, Complexity.Yap.Data.length_inst, Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_badLang, Complexity.Yap.Data.mem_innerLang, Complexity.Yap.Data.nLen, Complexity.Yap.length_le_of_query, Complexity.pairFstD, Complexity.pairFstD_pairEncode, Complexity.pairSndD, Complexity.pairSndD_pairEncode, Turing.pairEncode}

Let $d$ be a refutation data package and let $L_2,K$ be languages of Boolean strings.
Suppose that for every string $y$, membership in $L_2$ is equivalent to the existence of
a string $v$ with $|v|=M_2(y)$ and $\langle y,v\rangle\in K$. Suppose that for every
string $z$, nonmembership in $K$ is equivalent to the existence of a string $r$ with
$|r|\le C_3(|z|+1)^{c_3}$ and $\langle z,r\rangle\in R$. Assume that for all Boolean
strings $x,U,u,v,w,r$ with $|u|=M_1(x)$, $|v|\le M_2(\langle x,u\rangle)$, $|w|\le|U|$,
and $|r|\le C_3(nLen(x)+1)^{c_3}$, one has $|\langle\langle u,v\rangle,\langle
w,r\rangle\rangle|\le B(|\langle x,U\rangle|+1)^b$. If $\langle x,U\rangle$ belongs to
the inner language and $|u|=M_1(x)$, then $\langle x,u\rangle\in L_2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Collapse of the Polynomial Hierarchy]
\lean{Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly}
\label{Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly}
\leanok
\uses{Complexity.PH, Complexity.PH_eq_SigmaP_of_PiP_subset_SigmaP, Complexity.PiP_three_subset_SigmaP_three_of_coNP_subset_NPPoly, Complexity.SigmaP, Complexity.coNP, Language.InNPPoly}
\difficulty{1}
If every language in $\mathrm{coNP}$ is recognized by a polynomial-size family of
Boolean circuits with fan-in at most two, using existentially quantified auxiliary input
bits, then the polynomial hierarchy satisfies $\mathrm{PH}=\Sigma_3^P$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A Collapse of the Polynomial Hierarchy]
